title: Revisiting the design of selection systems in light of new findings regarding the validity of widely used predictors (Sackett, Zhang, Berry and Lievens, Industrial and Organizational Psychology 16, 2023)
supports: Revised validity estimates for selection methods (Table 1): structured interviews .42 with an 80% credibility interval of .18 to .66, job knowledge tests .40, empirically keyed biodata .38, work samples .33, cognitive ability .31 (later update .23), unstructured interviews .19; comparison with Schmidt and Hunter (1998).

title: A guide to structured interviewing for better hiring practices
supports: Parts of a structured interview (vetted questions with follow-ups, notes, rubrics rated poor to outstanding, interviewer training and calibration); behavioural and hypothetical questions; Google's internal findings of about 40 minutes saved per interview and rejected candidates reporting 35% higher satisfaction.

title: Evidence that gendered wording in job advertisements exists and sustains gender inequality (Gaucher, Friesen and Kay, JPSP 2011), study summary
publisher: Harvard Kennedy School, Gender Action Portal
supports: Masculine-coded wording in job ads lowered women's sense of belonging and the job's appeal without changing their view of their own skill; examples of masculine and feminine coded words; study sizes.

title: The effects of feedback interventions on performance: a historical review, a meta-analysis, and a preliminary feedback intervention theory (Kluger and DeNisi, Psychological Bulletin, 1996)
publisher: Hebrew University of Jerusalem research portal
supports: 607 effect sizes; average positive effect of feedback (d = .41); more than one third of feedback interventions lowered performance; feedback that shifts attention toward the self works less well.

title: Performance management: Could do better? (evidence review, 2016)
supports: Specific, challenging goals work for straightforward tasks and less for complex ones; feedback is needed for goals to work; appraisal reactions (fairness, usefulness) matter; keep development conversations separate from pay and promotion decisions.

title: Performance management factsheet
supports: Feedback should be regular, timely and focused on improvement; move away from forced ranking and heavy process toward ongoing reviews; behavioural or learning objectives for complex roles; dated 29 January 2026.

title: Employee engagement factsheet
supports: No single agreed definition of engagement; composite scores are hard to act on; combine surveys with focus groups; autonomy, manager support and voice as drivers; dated 23 July 2025.

title: Onboarding New Employees: Maximizing Success (Talya N. Bauer, SHRM Foundation Effective Practice Guidelines, 2010), copy hosted by the University of Georgia
supports: The Four Cs of onboarding (compliance, clarification, culture, connection); passive, high potential and proactive onboarding levels; new-hire adjustment levers (self-efficacy, role clarity, social integration, knowledge of culture).

title: Job Description Guide and Templates
supports: Five-step process for job descriptions; defining essential functions (requirement, frequency, consequence, alternatives, reassignment) to support ADA accommodation decisions; one standard format.

title: What the written statement must include
supports: UK principal statement items due on or before day one and items that can follow within two months (pensions, collective agreements, non-compulsory training, disciplinary and grievance rules); page updated 24 July 2025.

title: Acas Code of Practice on disciplinary and grievance procedures
supports: UK employers should follow a fair procedure in line with the Code; tribunals take procedure into account; Acas is consulting on an updated Code in 2026.

title: Plan to Make Work Pay and Employment Rights Act: timeline update
supports: Dates for Employment Rights Act 2025 measures (page updated 5 November 2026): SSP and day-one paternity leave 6 April 2026, Fair Work Agency 7 April 2026, tribunal time limit to 6 months 1 October 2026, harassment duty 30 October 2026, unfair dismissal qualifying period of 6 months from 1 January 2027, later measures in 2027, zero hours with no date.

title: Discrimination: your rights
supports: The protected characteristics under the Equality Act 2010 and that protection applies at work.

title: Inclusive language: words to use and avoid when writing about disability
supports: Words to use and avoid when writing about disability; let people self-identify; avoid victim language; page updated 17 June 2026.

title: Check a job applicant's right to work
supports: UK employers must check right to work before employment starts; keep copies for the employment plus 2 years; civil penalties; do not discriminate when checking.

title: Employment information (UK GDPR guidance and resources)
supports: ICO guidance areas for employers: keeping employment records, recruitment and selection, monitoring workers, workers' health information. Site blocks automated fetching; page confirmed through search results.

title: Prohibited Employment Policies/Practices
supports: US protected characteristics; job ads must not show a preference; word-of-mouth recruiting risk; no pre-offer disability questions; avoid asking for photos before an offer; equal pay.

title: Recordkeeping Requirements
supports: Keep personnel records one year (terminated staff: one year from termination); ADEA payroll records three years; Equal Pay Act records explaining pay differences two years; keep everything relevant once a charge is filed.

title: Background Checks: What Employers Need to Know
publisher: U.S. EEOC and Federal Trade Commission
supports: FCRA steps (stand-alone written notice, written permission, copy of report before adverse action, adverse action notice); apply the same standards to everyone.

title: Fact Sheet #21: Recordkeeping Requirements under the Fair Labor Standards Act
publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
supports: Records required for non-exempt workers; payroll records kept three years and wage computation records (time cards, schedules) two years; revised July 2008.

title: Last Paycheck
supports: No federal law requires immediate final pay; state laws may require faster payment.

title: I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification
supports: Every US employer completes Form I-9 for each hire; keep forms three years after hire or one year after termination, whichever is later; current edition dated 01/20/25.

title: Trump Administration Rescinds 2024 DOL White-Collar Overtime Expansion (14 May 2026)
supports: DOL rescinded the 2024 overtime rule effective 15 May 2026; federal exempt salary level $684 per week and highly compensated level $107,432; court history.

title: Several States Enact Pay Transparency Laws: What Employers Need to Know in 2026 (16 December 2025)
supports: US state pay-range posting laws and dates: California amendment 1 January 2026, New Jersey 1 June 2025, Vermont 1 July 2025, Massachusetts 29 October 2025 (25+ employees), Delaware 26 September 2027, Washington amendment 2025; Colorado (2021) and California (2023) as early laws.

title: EU Pay Transparency Directive 2026: employer compliance (1 July 2026)
supports: Transposition deadline 7 June 2026 and which member states had transposed; employer duties (pay range before interview, no pay history questions, right to information, reporting from 100 workers with first reports in June 2027, joint pay assessment at a 5% unexplained gap).

title: State of the Global Workplace: 2026 Report
supports: Global engagement 20% in 2025 data, 64% not engaged, 16% actively disengaged; US and Canada 31%; managers 22%; method and sample size; published April 2026.

title: Automated Employment Decision Tools (Local Law 144 of 2021)
publisher: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
supports: Bias audit within one year of use, public summary of results, notice to candidates 10 business days before use; enforcement from 5 July 2023.

title: EU Digital Omnibus on AI Enters Into Force (31 July 2026)
supports: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 published 24 July 2026, in force 27 July 2026; Annex III high-risk AI, including employment uses, moved from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027; transparency duties still apply from 2 August 2026.

title: O*NET OnLine Help: Summary Report
publisher: O*NET (U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration)
supports: What an O*NET occupation report contains: tasks, technology skills, work activities, skills, knowledge, education, wages and employment trends.

title: Code of Practice on disciplinary and grievance procedures (full text, 2015)
supports: Disciplinary steps (establish facts, inform in writing, meeting, right to be accompanied, decide and confirm in writing, appeal) and grievance steps; tribunals can adjust awards by up to 25% for unreasonable failure to follow the Code; in effect since 11 March 2015.
